knowledge:
- key_parameters: fdr.cutoff=Used in estimateBackground to set the False Discovery Rate threshold for identifying regions expressed significantly above background noise ;; gap.dist.range=A vector of gap distances tested in estimateGapDistance to find the optimal distance for merging adjacent transcribed fragments ;; min.overlap=Used in annotateTranscripts to control the minimal proportion of overlap required to associate a detected transcript with a reference annotation ;; reduce.peaks=Logical parameter in constructCDS; if TRUE, merges neighboring peaks to prevent artificial transcript truncation caused by peak-calling algorithms splitting broad peaks ;; gapwidth=Used in constructCDS to define the minimum gap distance below which neighboring ChIP-seq peaks are merged ;; quant.cutoff=Used in predictStrand to filter out ChIP-seq peaks with RNA-seq coverage below the specified quantile threshold ;; win.size=Flanking region size used in predictStrand to calculate RNA-seq read densities upstream and downstream of the TSS
- alternatives: mRNA-seq is mentioned as an alternative sequencing method, but it is preferred for steady-state mature transcript levels and splice variants, whereas GRO-seq, nucRNA-seq, and chrRNA-seq are preferred for primary de novo transcription profiling. Peak calling algorithms like MACS2 are used externally to generate the input peak files for the ChIP-seq workflow.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have strand-specific nascent or nuclear RNA-seq data (GRO-seq, nucRNA-seq, chrRNA-seq) and want to computationally identify and quantify primary transcripts, especially when you also have complementary ChIP-seq data (e.g., H3K4me3 or H3K9ac) to resolve overlapping or closely spaced transcription units.
- pitfalls: Low mappability and repeat regions can create artificial gaps in RNA-seq coverage, segmenting single transcripts into multiple fragments; this must be corrected by tuning the gap distance parameter. Peak-calling algorithms often split broad ChIP-seq peaks into multiple narrow peaks, which can lead to false positives and unnecessary transcript truncation if reduce.peaks is not set to TRUE. Not all ChIP-seq peaks represent active transcription; a classification model (predictTssOverlap) must be used to filter out background peaks.

workflows.name: rna_seq_only_transcript_detection
workflows.intent: Detect, annotate, and quantify de novo primary transcripts from strand-specific RNA-seq data alone.
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the TranscriptionDataSet object ;; 2. Estimate expression background noise level ;; 3. Estimate the optimal gap distance for merging fragmented transcripts ;; 4. Call transcripts using the estimated parameters ;; 5. Annotate detected transcripts against reference genes ;; 6. Retrieve and export transcripts to BED format
workflows.code:
tds <- constructTDS(file = path.to.Bam, region = region, fragment.size = 250, unique = FALSE, paired.end = FALSE, swap.strand = TRUE)
estimateBackground(tds, fdr.cutoff = 0.01)
gd <- seq(from = 0, to = 10000, by = 100)
estimateGapDistance(object = tds, annot = knownGene.genes, filter.annot = TRUE, fpkm.quantile = 0.25, gap.dist.range = gd)
detectTranscripts(tds, estimate.params = TRUE)
annotateTranscripts(object = tds, annot = knownGene.genes, min.overlap = 0.5)
trx <- getTranscripts(tds, min.length = 250, min.fpkm = 0.5)
transcriptsToBed(object = trx, file = "transcripts.bed", strand.color = c("blue", "red"))

workflows.name: integrated_rna_and_chip_seq_demarcation
workflows.intent: Integrate RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data to classify active transcription start sites and demarcate individual transcript boundaries.
input: path.to.peaks (ChIP-seq peak file, e.g., MACS2 output)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize and run the RNA-seq transcript detection workflow ;; 2. Construct the ChipDataSet object and evaluate peak genomic distribution ;; 3. Predict gene-associated ChIP-seq peaks using a logistic regression model ;; 4. Predict peak strandedness by analyzing upstream/downstream RNA-seq read densities ;; 5. Demarcate transcript boundaries by breaking closely spaced transcripts using active peaks ;; 6. Re-annotate and retrieve the final set of resolved transcripts
workflows.code:
tds <- constructTDS(file = path.to.Bam, region = region, fragment.size = 250, unique = FALSE, paired.end = FALSE, swap.strand = TRUE)
estimateBackground(tds, fdr.cutoff = 0.01)
gd <- seq(from = 0, to = 10000, by = 100)
estimateGapDistance(object = tds, annot = knownGene.genes, filter.annot = TRUE, fpkm.quantile = 0.25, gap.dist.range = gd)
detectTranscripts(tds, estimate.params = TRUE)
cds <- constructCDS(peaks = path.to.peaks, reads = path.to.reads, region = region, TxDb = knownGene, tssOf = "transcript", tss.region = c(-2000, 2000), reduce.peaks = TRUE, gapwidth = 500, unique = TRUE, swap.strand = FALSE)
predictTssOverlap(object = cds, feature = "pileup", p = 0.75)
predictStrand(cdsObj = cds, tdsObj = tds, quant.cutoff = 0.1, win.size = 2000)
breakTranscriptsByPeaks(tdsObj = tds, cdsObj = cds, estimate.params = TRUE)
annotateTranscripts(object = tds, annot = knownGene.genes, min.overlap = 0.5)
trx.final <- getTranscripts(tds)
transcriptsToBed(object = trx.final, file = "transcripts_final.bed")
